title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness & starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness and reduce request starvation; added starvation timeout/backstop, metrics and feature flags for gradual rollout.
description:
Motivation: production traces and perf-canary runs showed persistent tail latency for small, low-priority requests under heavy load. The continuous-batcher scheduler could favor large batching windows and high-throughput workloads, causing long wait times (starvation) for short requests and interactive traffic. This PR implements scheduler-side mitigations: queueing fairness buckets, per-request starvation timers with a configurable timeout/backstop, age-based bypass to prevent indefinite waiting, and telemetry to monitor queue age and fairness.

What I changed: tuned scheduler heuristics and added new config knobs (bucket_count, queue_starvation_timeout_ms, age_bypass_threshold_ms), introduced a lightweight token-credit mechanism to ensure per-queue fairness, and added end-to-end unit/integration tests that simulate mixed workloads. Also added new Prometheus metrics: continuous_batcher_queue_age_seconds, queue_starvations_total, queue_fair_shares, queue_age_bypass_total. The change is behind a feature flag `scheduler_fairness_v2` for gradual rollout.

Compatibility: the default config keeps current behavior; enabling the feature flag applies the new fairness logic and timeouts. No changes to public API.

Testing: local unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, and a staged rollout on a subset of dedicated capacity. Perf-canary showed a 35% reduction in 99th percentile latency for small requests under a mixed workload and eliminated observed request waits > 2s in the test harness.

Rollout plan: enable feature flag in perf-canary, monitor the new metrics and circuit-breaker alerts for 48h, then ramp to 20% of traffic, with capability to revert by disabling the flag.

Related: ENG-9243 (fairness improvements), ENG-9301 (kv-cache interaction follow-up), SUP-4421 (customer incident where short requests were starved).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain the token-credit math for multi-tenant pools? I want to ensure we don't unfairly throttle a customer with bursty single-request patterns.

Ava Martinez: Reply: token credits are proportional to recent throughput-weighted shares with a floor per-tenant to avoid starvation. Added a comment in token_allocator.rs and expanded unit tests to cover bursty single-request flows.
